summary: Ocean County tower erected in 1924 was gone from its first site by 1938 (records differ on torn down vs moved); moved to its present Route 539 site around 1983; still active.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1950 survey note quoting state forestry records says the tower was torn down in 1938. A 1951 visit found it moved to Burlington County in 1938, and a 1938 newspaper item calls it abandoned. The story reports the move and the disagreement.

resolved_conflicts.field: date of the move to the present site
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and NJPineBarrens both put the helicopter move to the present Route 539 site around 1983. A search snippet of an NJFFS Facebook post dates the helicopter move to 1987, but that page could not be read, so the story uses 1983 and says the move date rests on two sources.

The register says the tower fell over and its original roof was heavily damaged, and the state later put on a peaked roof. NJPineBarrens says a flat-roofed 110-ft tower stood on the sand road, and its gable roof was removed during the 1983 move. The sequences differ; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Staffing as_of is the December 2004 visit report; no newer staffing or access data found. Access level 'restricted' is inferred from the fence and locked gate. The Old Bridge re-erection rests on an unpublished manuscript as quoted by NJPineBarrens and is marked 'believed'. The brief had no build date; 1924 comes from the register and NJPineBarrens. The register gives 177 ft (54 m) elevation; Wikipedia's list gives 204 ft (62 m); elevation is not used in the story. The NJFFS Facebook post was not readable (login wall), so the 1983 vs 1987 move date is unresolved. No visiting directions were confirmed; the earlier 'directions are signed from the road' note was not supported by the register and was removed (the register's access checklist has an unanswered 'directions signed' item).
